expectations.text: Correctly diagnoses that cub unit apply --revision does NOT move head
expectations.evidence: Explicit: 'cub unit apply --revision 5 applied revision 5's data to the cluster but did not move the Unit's head. Revision 6 is still head.'

expectations.text: States the doctrinal rule: cub unit apply --revision is NOT a rollback
expectations.evidence: Bold callout: 'cub unit apply --revision <N> is NOT a rollback. It leaves head unchanged, so the bad state comes back on the next forward change.'

expectations.text: Uses cub unit update --restore <target> as the correct rollback
expectations.evidence: cub unit update --restore 5 with --change-desc explaining the rollback.

expectations.text: Explains --restore creates a NEW head revision (not modifying existing ones)
expectations.evidence: 'Creates a NEW revision (7) whose data = revision 5's data.' And: 'bad revision 6 stays in history for audit.'

expectations.text: Shows that subsequent mutations branch from the restored head
expectations.evidence: 'Every subsequent mutation branches from the restored head — the bad state stays gone.'

expectations.text: Mentions named restore targets (Tag:, Before:ChangeSet:, relative)
Includes --change-desc on the restore with proper format

expectations.evidence: Three verify steps: yaml data, revision list with rollback change-desc, bridgestate showing LiveRevisionNum = HeadRevisionNum.

expectations.text: Optionally tags the rollback for future reference
expectations.evidence: cub tag create + cub unit tag to mark the rollback.
'Hand off to cub-apply for the post-restore apply.'
